frames.narration: A support assistant sends each question with an 800-token prompt: 600 tokens of shared system prompt and policy text, then about 200 tokens of customer question. A large-model call costs about $0.0047 and takes about 2 s, so the gateway checks a cache first.
Miss: the cache embeds the question (about 40 ms) and finds nothing within the 0.95 similarity threshold. The request goes to the router.
The router tries the small model first: about $0.0002 and 0.6 s. Its confidence is 92, above the escalation limit of 65, so the answer is accepted and stored in the cache for tenant A.
Later a tenant A customer asks "What is your refund window?". The embedding is 0.98 similar to the stored question, which is over 0.95. Hit in 5 ms for about $0, no model call.

Danger: "Refund if I cancel within 3 days?" is a different question but its embedding is 0.97 similar, so it is also a hit and gets the stored 30-day answer. Nothing flags it. A threshold of 0.99 would have caught this one but also missed real paraphrases.
A hard question (tax proration on an upgrade) misses the cache. The small model answers with confidence 40, below 65, so the router escalates: total $0.0002 + $0.0047 = about $0.0049 and 2.6 s.
The large model's provider starts returning 429s. The router fails over to a second provider for the same model class, or to the small model with a note, instead of an error.

A tenant B customer asks "Which plan limits apply to me?". Cache entries are scoped by tenant, so tenant A's answer is never served: this is a miss and goes to the models. Without that scope it would be a data leak.
